beginner_short.label: Beginner team, limited time (< 2 hours)
stack: HTML + CSS + vanilla JavaScript for the frontend — no framework overhead
Python with Flask for the backend — minimal boilerplate, great for prototyping
JSON files or in-memory dictionaries for data — no database setup needed
Free APIs (Groq, OpenAI free tier) for AI features — avoid complex ML pipelines
beginner_short.rationale: Minimize moving parts. Every new technology is a potential debugging sinkhole under time pressure. Stick to what the team already knows.

beginner_long.label: Beginner team, more time (3+ hours)
stack: React (Create React App or Vite) for a more structured frontend
Node.js with Express or Python with Flask for the backend
SQLite or JSON file storage for simple persistence
One external API for the core AI/data feature
beginner_long.rationale: With more time, a lightweight framework adds structure without overwhelming beginners. But still avoid over-engineering — one framework per layer is enough.

intermediate_short.label: Intermediate team, limited time (< 2 hours)
stack: React or Vue.js for the frontend — use whichever the team already knows
Flask or FastAPI for the backend — FastAPI if the team wants async
In-memory storage or SQLite — no remote database setup
Groq or OpenAI API for AI features with a rule-based fallback
intermediate_short.rationale: Intermediate teams can handle a framework but should still avoid setup-heavy tools. Speed comes from using familiar tech, not new tech.

intermediate_long.label: Intermediate team, more time (3+ hours)
stack: React/Next.js or Vue/Nuxt for frontend with routing
Node.js/Express or Python/FastAPI for the backend
MongoDB Atlas (free tier) or PostgreSQL for persistence
LLM API with structured output (JSON mode) + vector search if relevant
intermediate_long.rationale: With time and experience, teams can set up a fuller stack. But prioritize the demo flow over infrastructure — a working end-to-end beats a sophisticated backend nobody sees.

advanced_short.label: Advanced team, limited time
stack: Whatever frontend framework the team is fastest with
FastAPI or Flask for rapid backend iteration
Pre-trained models (HuggingFace, spaCy) instead of training from scratch
Docker if the team has a boilerplate ready — otherwise skip it
advanced_short.rationale: Advanced teams should resist the urge to build complex infrastructure. The jury sees the demo, not the architecture. Use pre-built components aggressively.

general_advice: Use what you already know — a hackathon is not the time to learn a new framework
Every technology choice should survive the question: 'Can we debug this in 10 minutes if it breaks?'
If you're debating between two options for more than 2 minutes, pick the simpler one
Free tiers and local hosting are your friends — don't waste time on deployment
Have a fallback for every external dependency (API down? Use a hardcoded response)
